# **31**<sup>**st**</sup> **August – 11**<sup>**th**</sup> **September 2009 SHFE prices fluctuate along with anxiety about weak fundamentals and China’s monetary policies** 

More concerns have been raised on fundamentals in the past two weeks, and copper prices have shown less momentum to go up. Both LME and SHFE inventory stocks have increased since August, showing weak fundamentals in both domestic and global market. SHFE inventory stocks rose for a seventh consecutive week and reached a new record since July 2007. The domestic spot premium fell from RMB 100/t and a discount of RMB 150/t last week, and stabilised at a discount of RMB 150-0/t this week. 



SHFE cash prices dropped below RMB 48,000/t last week due to the rumour that the new loan approvals in August would drop year-on-year.  SHFE prices bounced back on 2<sup>nd</sup> Sep when the China Securities Regulatory Commission addressed the importance of enhancing the steadiness of the market. Although the Central Bank announced that it is to maintain the loose monetary policy with only moderate regulation, the worries of lower liquidity have been proved as July’s new loan figure has significantly shrank, and the

The uncertainty of China’s monetary policies will continue until the August figure is released, although it is fairly certain that it will hardly reach RMB 500 billion ($73 billion) as expected earlier. Without strong factors from either supply or demand side, it is believed that SHFE cash prices will stay between RMB 48,000-52,000/t over the next couple of weeks. 

# **Demand for scrap rises as spot TC/RCs remain low** 

China’s refined copper output in August reached 364,900 tonnes and up by 15.4% against last year, which has put more pressure on raw material purchasing. China has replaced Japan as the second largest importer of copper concentrate of the world since 2008, and will remain as an important buyer in the concentrate market, considering all the new smelting capacity in the next couple of years. The Chinese government has recently announced that it will support copper concentrate imports by offering importers a subsidy. In China, spot TC/RCs are heard under $10/1¢, indicating a tight supply of copper concentrates on the market. However, the availability of scrap has eased such pressure since July. According to newly released data, China’s scrap import dropped to around 390,000t in August but still maintained at a high level. CRU has been told by some large smelters that scrap has largely replaced concentrates since August, and that two of them will only purchase limited amount of concentrates until the end of this year. Hence, scrap traders have been reluctant to move downwards with copper price in the last week. It is believed that more scrap is required to meet smelter’s demand, although the su

pply may tighten again after October according to some traders. # **Cathodes import at a loss as the** # **SHFE/LME ratio falls** The SHFE/LME ratio stays at a low rate and the loss of cathode trading continues, therefore the consumption has largely relied on domestic stocks. China’s imports of unwrought copper and semifinished copper products fell to 325,098 tonnes in August and its refined copper import is estimated to drop to around 230,000t. Taking the lag effect into consideration, CRU suspects that China’s refined copper import may fall to a lower level in the next month. Both premiums for imported cathodes and SXEW cathodes slid down a little, to a level of $70-90 and $50-70 respectively. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **September 2009** www.crumonitor.com # **Consumptions diverge among recovery hopes** In general, the light season for copper is approaching the end, and the demand will pick up from late September or early October. The demand for copper in power and telecom industries remains stable, and three major semi-copper processors reported that they have received increased orders in September and have all been operating at above 80-85% of their capacity since August. China’s automobile’s sales in August reached above 1.1 million, up by 80% from the last year, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. The NDRC forecasted that China’s automobile sales may increase 28% yearon-year and the copper consumption in auto industry is expected to rise accordingly. The demand for copper tubes used in domestic appliances, however, is declining as its delayed light season finally comes. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **John Tomlinson (London):** +44 20 7903 2103 john.tomlinson@crugroup.com **Paul Settles (London):** +44 20 7903 2227 paul.settles@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 11th September 2009.
